LFR firefighter Kasey Davis, also Ropesville fire chief, says Churchill quote about ‘what we give’ sums up his life well

by adminAugust 18, 2026August 18, 2026

Department: Lubbock Fire Rescue

Name: Kasey Davis

Rank: Firefighter

How long with department: 15½ years

Listen to audio version of this article
0:00 / 1:56
Instaread

Roles: Medical instructor, fire instructor, scuba instructor, Honor Guard member.

Hometown: Ropesville

Education (high school, college/degrees): Three Way High School in Maple, northwest of Morton.

Spouse: Married 15 years

Children: Three boys

Why did you choose this profession? I’ve always been someone who likes doing things for people. I did electronics construction for residential and commercial jobs – electronics, wiring and stuff. But I got tired of it. I went into Station 14 and asked the guys if they like their jobs and they said they love their job. Everyone said it at same time. I had no fire background – I grew up on a farm – but I started pursuing it because it would give me a reason to go to work.

How do you deal with stressful situations? It’s different now than when I was younger. I learn how to take a stressful situation/problem and figure out how to break it down, how to fix and solve. One step at a time to make the situation better. Learned a lot from my peers and veterans on how to compartmentalize and get through it. I also work with a counselor to have a baseline and not take it home. And being home with my family also helps.

Honors/highlights: Honor Guard is a big thing for firefighters who’ve died. Public education with kids. And last August I also became fire chief for Ropesville after it was shut down in 2011.

Hobbies & interests: Jujitsu. Traveling and seeing different parts of the country as a family. Building things at home – I’m a handyman. Fishing and hiking.

Community involvement beyond work: Substitute at school to give back and do CPR training classes.

Quote: “We make a living by what we get, but we make a life by what we give,” – Winston Churchill
